text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The engineering, procurement and construction contract to build the Bakun hydro-electric dam was signed on Wednesday after three postponements with Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad expressing confidence that it would be completed in five years.

- Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance Anwar Ibrahim yesterday expressed Malaysia's concern over the tendency of the International Monetary Fund in the past few years to apply different standards in its treatment of member countries.

- With time running out, Batu member of parliament Joseph Chong continues to explore legal avenues to enable him to contest the Gerakan party elections on Saturday when he filed another application at the High Court on Wednesday.

- United Malays National Organisation members found to have been involved in money politics in the run-up to the party's election next week will also risk jeopardising their party positions outside the party, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad says.

- Going short on the Kuala Lumpur stock market under the recently allowed regulated short-selling is proving easier said than done. Three days after kicking off the activity, no volume has yet to be recorded.

- A multimedia university complete with state-of-the-art technology features will be built along the proposed multimedia super corridor highway linking Kuala Lumpur with the proposed Putrajaya administrative centre and the Kuala Lumpur international airport.
